title: Troubleshooting Method: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: Something on the network is broken. Most people start guessing. Good engineers start at the bottom.

scenes.heading: The car mechanic
scenes.narration: A mechanic checks the simple things first. Start at layer one, the cables and the link lights. Then layer two, such as V L A Ns and trunks. Then layer three, addresses and routes. Work up one layer at a time until you find it.

scenes.heading: Go-to commands
scenes.narration: A few commands cover most checks. Check the interface. Check the V L A N. Check the trunk. And check the route.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three traps. Up up can still hide errors. A ping doesn't prove everything works. Reboot is a last resort.

items.wrong: A good ping means all is well

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Start at layer one and work up. Check interfaces, V L A Ns, trunks and routes. Never reboot first. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva troubleshooting lab.
